title: The Boltzmann–Grad limit throughout a regular kinetic lifespan
exact_target: For the specified stable radial finite-range Newtonian potentials in three dimensions, including the allowed attractive wells, and C1 initial probability density with Gaussian bounds on it and its spatial gradient, assume the associated Boltzmann equation has a nonnegative classical solution uniformly Gaussian-bounded on [0,T]. Does the conditioned product grand-canonical Newtonian gas at Boltzmann–Grad activity $\epsilon ^{-2}$ have every fixed scaled s-particle factorial density converge to $f(t)^tensor-s$ in L1 uniformly on [0,T]?
